title: Client
content: Overview ACP::Client manages the ACP v1 lifecycle. It handles request correlation and dispatches incoming messages via a background fiber. ACP v2 Preview Use ACP::V2::Client with an existing transport, or ACP::V2.connect to start and initialize an Agent subprocess. Use ACP::Client or ACP.connect for v1 Agents. A v2 connection raises VersionMismatchError when the Agent selects a different version. client = ACP::V2::Client.new(ACP::ProcessTransport.new("my-agent")) client.on_update = ->(note : ACP::Protocol::V2::SessionUpdateParams) do if chunk = note.update.typed.as?(ACP::Protocol::V2::MessageChunkUpdate) print chunk.to_content_chunk.try(&.text) end nil end begin client.initialize_connection session = client.session_new(Dir.current) inserted = client.session_prompt_text(session.session_id, "Summarize this project") puts "Inserted message #{inserted.message_id}" # Continue reading session updates until your application is done. ensure client.close end The prompt response acknowledges insertion and carries the inserted user message's ID. Foreground completion arrives in an idle state_update. Keep on_update callbacks short because they run on the dispatcher fiber. ACP v2 prompt acceptance For initialize_connection in either protocol version, pass meta: as a Hash(String, JSON::Any) or a Protocol::RawJson object. Use meta_raw on the implementation info to supply exact _meta values there as well. Stdio preserves the original numbers on the wire. Capability objects also expose meta_raw for exact extension values on either side of the handshake. When repeating the v2 handshake, omitting meta: reuses the last successful offer and meta: nil clears it. ACP v2 Initialization Session creation and fork responses in both versions, and v2 prompt acknowledgements, expose exact extension metadata via meta_raw. An ambiguous returned ID or repeated JSON-RPC result raises ProtocolError. New sessions must also have IDs distinct from existing sessions. ACP v1 session setup ACP v2 session setup ACP v2 prompts accept baseline text and resource links. Images, audio, embedded resources, and skill references require their respective grants. For custom content, set client.on_prompt_content_type to check the Agent’s advertised capabilities against the extension’s documented rules. The callback receives the custom type and the Agent’s capability object. Stdio preserves the exact JSON values in the advertisement. client.on_prompt_content_type = ->(type : String, agent : ACP::Protocol::RawJson) do meta = agent.field("session").try(&.field("prompt")).try(&.field("_meta")) type == "_example.test/diagram" && meta.try(&.field("example.test/diagrams")).try(&.json) == "true" end This example uses an extension that advertises a boolean under prompt capability metadata. The extension defines its own key, location, and value. Return true only when the Agent advertises support for that type. ACP v2 Prompt Content Use note.raw from the v2 update callback to store or forward notification parameters. It preserves unknown fields and exact JSON numbers over stdio, including in updates whose typed accessor returns nil. The notification's meta exposes fields representable as JSON::Any. Use meta_raw for the whole metadata object. Custom transports can supply Protocol::WireFrame from receive_frame to retain exact values. ACP v2 Session Updates Use session_state(session_id) to read the latest foreground and background snapshot for an attached root session. A new session starts at idle until the Agent reports activity. A resume uses the Agent's current snapshot. A newly attached session with no usable resume snapshot reports unknown. background is nil when unreported and empty when the Agent reports no background work. Check idle? before interpreting a stop reason. Use subagent(session_id) for a child session's state. The snapshot is available from on_update once its session is attached. session_state_raw(session_id) preserves extension fields and exact JSON numbers over stdio. Closing or deleting the session clears the snapshot. ACP v2 Session States The v2 client supports session creation, listing, resume and replay, prompts, configuration changes, close and delete. Register on_request_permission and on_create_elicitation to handle Agent requests. Authentication is available through auth_login, auth_logout, and authenticate_terminal. Pass Protocol::V2::AuthLoginParams or Protocol::V2::AuthLogoutParams to send authentication request metadata. Set meta_raw on the parameters or read it on the result to preserve exact JSON values. Use meta_raw on the initialize result or an advertised authentication method to read exact extension values from the Agent. Use tool_call_cancel and terminal_cancel when the entity announces a current cancel capability. ACP v2 Prompt Lifecycle Return RequestPermissionResult.selected(option_id) for an option from the request or RequestPermissionResult.cancelled when no option was chosen. An invalid result or selection returns JSON-RPC -32603 to the Agent. Over stdio, repeated permission option fields return -32602 before the callback runs. Set outcome_raw for a custom or future outcome with exact JSON and meta_raw for exact metadata on the result. ACP v2 Permissions on_elicitation_complete fires once for each accepted URL elicitation on the connection. A completion that arrives before the accept reply is sent is held until the reply is written successfully. Completion callbacks run on the dispatcher. If no typed handler is set, matching notifications that fit in JSON::Any go to on_notification. The typed completion exposes exact metadata through meta_raw. ACP v2 URL Completion Both protocol versions require an elicitation scope and a message. URL mode also requires an absolute URL and an opaque elicitationId. The client returns JSON-RPC -32602 for invalid requests before calling the handler. ACP v1 accepts an explicit null request ID for request scope. ACP v1 Elicitation Scope Typed form and URL requests expose exact extension metadata through meta_raw. Use CreateElicitationResult#meta_raw= to return exact metadata or copy it from a request. The meta accessor provides editable JSON object fields. Edits to objects and arrays preserve untouched wire values, including nested entries moved within an array. Scalar matches prefer their original positions. Use meta_raw= to distinguish numbers that project to the same value or to replace an array that contains unrepresentable scalars. Stdio supports exact replies. A custom transport that cannot preserve an exact reply returns JSON-RPC -32603 to the Agent. ACP Extension Metadata An ACP v2 elicitation with request_id belongs to an outstanding Client request on the same connection. The client rejects a request-scoped elicitation with toolCallId. The callback's local cancellation channel closes when the elicitation is cancelled, its originating request ends before an input reply is sent, or the connection closes. Use the channel to dismiss a form or URL consent prompt that is still open. ACP v2 Elicitation For v2 form elicitations, requested_schema contains the supported controls. An optional control of an unsupported type is omitted. A form with a missing or unsupported required control, or a malformed standard control, returns JSON-RPC -32602 before the callback runs. Use requested_schema_raw for the original schema. In both versions, the typed schema, properties, and choices expose exact meta_raw. Numeric fields expose minimum_raw, maximum_raw, and default_raw alongside the ordinary numeric accessors. Render text fields with unrecognized format values as plain text. ACP v2 Form Mode For accepted forms, the client checks submitted field names, required fields, types, choices, bounds, and the email, uri, date, and date-time string formats against the original schema. Format checks are local syntax checks. Leap seconds are checked for possible placement at the end of a UTC month. A callback that supplies invalid form content causes a JSON-RPC -32603 reply to the Agent. Use CreateElicitationResult.accept_raw with a Protocol::RawJson content object to submit exact numbers in either version or values for declared custom fields in v2. Stdio supports exact frames. Custom transports can override send_wire to add that support. ACP v2 Elicitation Responses ACP v1 form callbacks also validate submissions against the original schema. The schema type and property map retain their v1 defaults. V1 date-time uses ISO 8601. V1 pattern translates common ECMAScript character classes and Unicode escapes and uses Crystal's regex engine with bounded matching. A v1 client using its generic Agent request callback can return the same form replies as a typed handler. Invalid submissions return -32603 to the Agent. ACP v1 Elicitation For session_prompt, supply at least one content block. An optional idempotency_key must contain 1 to 255 characters. Set meta_raw on ACP::Protocol::V2::SessionPromptParams to send exact extension metadata. Session setup requires absolute Agent paths, unique MCP server names, and an absolute executable path for each stdio server. Invalid arguments raise ArgumentError before the client sends the request. ACP v2 Session Setup Read the latest configuration with session_config_options(session_id). It returns an empty list when an attached session offers no options, and nil when the client has no snapshot for that session. Use session_config_options_raw(session_id) for the exact option list, including extension fields and precise numbers. session_set_config_option checks the Agent's current option IDs and advertised select values before sending. ACP v2 Session Config Options Read the current command list with session_available_commands(session_id). Filter by slash_command? to build slash command completion. The list is empty when the session has no commands and nil when the client has no snapshot for the session. Ambiguous command names are omitted from the typed list. Setup responses and available_commands_update notifications replace the list. Read it inside on_update to see the latest live replacement. With the stdio transport, session_available_commands_raw(session_id) retains extension variants and exact numeric values. After a close, archive, or delete timeout, the list is unavailable until the Agent confirms the request failed or a successful resume supplies a new list. ACP v2 Slash Commands In a permission callback, typed_subject exposes the optional tool-call patch or command details. Use subject_raw for exact JSON, including future subjects and values outside JSON::Any. The request, subject, and command details expose exact extension metadata through meta_raw. Tool-call patches also expose raw_input_raw, raw_output_raw, and meta_raw. Changes to a JSON::Any array are serialized from that view at its numeric precision. A tool-call patch from a permission request reaches on_update in receive order before the permission handler runs. Use the callback's request_id to match $/cancel_request notifications delivered through on_notification. ACP v2 Permission Requests Session info and usage Use a SessionDetailsStore per connection to retain the session info and context-window usage reported through on_update. details = ACP::V2::SessionDetailsStore.new client.on_update = ->(update : ACP::Protocol::V2::SessionUpdateParams) do details.observe(update) nil end info = details.session_info(session_id) usage = details.session_usage(session_id) Both lookups return nil until their first usable update. Session info patches the title, RFC 3339 activity time, and metadata. Usage updates replace the token counts and patch the cumulative cost and usage metadata. cost_raw preserves the Agent's exact JSON amount. cost provides a Float64 projection. A parent's reported cost already includes its descendants' cost. The store defaults to 128 sessions and 64 KiB of retained detail data per session. Adjust session_limit: and session_byte_limit:, or pass nil to remove a limit. The store keeps the latest token counts and applies cost and usage metadata that fit. It preserves explicit clears when a different usage field exceeds the budget. When the Agent sends current details on resume, it sends them after any requested replay. Use forget_session when you stop retaining details for a session. ACP v2 session info · ACP v2 usage · Current-state synchronization Session compaction Feed each connection's v2 session updates to a CompactionStore in receive order. Compaction updates are available without a v2 capability. compactions = ACP::V2::CompactionStore.new client.on_update = ->(update : ACP::Protocol::V2::SessionUpdateParams) do compactions.observe(update) nil end snapshot = compactions.compaction(session_id, compaction_id) compactions(session_id) lists retained entries in first-seen order. The snapshot has the current status, error, and exact meta_raw. Read summary_raw for exact blocks or summary_blocks for usable display blocks. A summary replacement clears or replaces the accumulated blocks. Chunk metadata stays on the incoming CompactionSummaryChunkUpdate. The store defaults to 128 compactions across sessions and 256 KiB per entry. Adjust compaction_limit: and compaction_byte_limit:, or pass nil to remove a limit. summary_incomplete? flags a gap caused by the byte limit. An accepted summary replacement clears the gap and resumes appending chunks. When a replacement summary exceeds the budget, the store can still retain the status, error, and metadata that fit. An update can also retain a new status and summary with earlier details if the new error or metadata would exceed the budget. Use forget_session to discard one session's compactions. To reconstruct a view from full replay, collect its updates in a fresh store and use each session's own replay_complete to track delivery. The configured limits apply to replayed updates. ACP v2 session compaction · Replay completion Transcript messages Feed each connection's v2 session updates to a MessageStore in receive order. User, Agent, thought, and session-directed messages have independent ID scopes within each session. transcript = ACP::V2::MessageStore.new client.on_update = ->(update : ACP::Protocol::V2::SessionUpdateParams) do transcript.observe(update) nil end message = transcript.message(session_id, ACP::V2::MessageKind::Agent, message_id) messages(session_id) lists retained messages in first-seen order. Use content_raw for exact blocks, content_blocks to decode usable display blocks, and skill_references for draft skill references in user messages. Message updates patch meta_raw by key. Chunk metadata remains available on the incoming MessageChunkUpdate. Session-directed messages expose the reported sender and recipient session and message IDs. The store defaults to 512 messages across sessions and 256 KiB per message for IDs, links, metadata, content, and streamed block storage. Adjust message_limit: and message_byte_limit:, or pass nil to remove a limit. At the message count limit, observe returns false for a new message ID. observe returns true when an update applies or records a content gap. Use content_incomplete? to show that content exceeded the byte limit. An oversized replacement clears earlier content, and an oversized chunk leaves the retained prefix. A full content replacement clears the gap and resumes appending chunks. A replacement can fit while new links or metadata exceed the remaining budget. In that case the new content is retained with the previous links and metadata. For a full replay, use forget_session on the affected sessions or collect replay into a fresh store. Each session's replay_complete marks the end of the Agent's replay delivery. The store's configured limits still apply to those updates. ACP v2 message updates · Replay completion Plan state Feed each connection's v2 session updates to a PlanStore in receive order. A plan_update replaces the complete plan with that ID in its session. plans = ACP::V2::PlanStore.new client.on_update = ->(update : ACP::Protocol::V2::SessionUpdateParams) do plans.observe(update) nil end snapshot = plans.plan(session_id, plan_id) current = snapshot.try(&.plan.typed) plans(session_id) lists retained snapshots. plan_raw keeps exact JSON for checklist, Markdown, and extension plans. meta_raw holds metadata from the update envelope. A removal deletes the corresponding snapshot. The store defaults to 128 plans across sessions and 256 KiB of serialized state per plan. Set plan_limit: or plan_byte_limit: to change a limit, or pass nil to remove it. observe returns true when an update stores or discards a snapshot. An oversized replacement discards any previous snapshot with that ID so the display can clear outdated content. Use forget_session to discard one session's plan state. To rebuild from full replay while keeping the current view available, feed the replay into a fresh store and switch each session's view after its own replay_complete. ACP v2 plan updates · Replay completion Tool-call state Create a ToolCallStore per connection and feed it v2 session updates in receive order. The client sends permission tool-call patches through the same on_update callback before it calls on_request_permission. tool_calls = ACP::V2::ToolCallStore.new client.on_update = ->(update : ACP::Protocol::V2::SessionUpdateParams) do tool_calls.observe(update) nil end call = tool_calls.tool_call(session_id, tool_call_id) Snapshots contain the current fields, exact JSON for raw input and output, and detached content in receive order. A content patch replaces the list. Chunks append to it. Content-item metadata stays on the item. Read chunk-scoped metadata from ToolCallContentChunk#meta_raw in the callback. Use the snapshot for display and client.tool_call_cancel for live cancellation checks. When presenting a permission prompt, use the RequestPermissionParams delivered to that permission callback. By default, the store retains up to 128 calls across sessions and up to 1 MiB of serialized state per call. Set call_limit: or call_byte_limit: to change the corresponding limit, or pass nil to remove it. observe returns false when an update would exceed either limit or a tool-call patch repeats a recognized field. The stored state remains intact in either case. Use forget_session to discard one session's tool-call history. For full replay of a session tree, clear all affected sessions first or use a fresh store. ACP v2 tool-call updates Display-only terminal state Create a TerminalStore per connection and feed it v2 session updates in receive order. Look up terminals by the reporting session and terminal IDs. terminals = ACP::V2::TerminalStore.new client.on_update = ->(update : ACP::Protocol::V2::SessionUpdateParams) do terminals.observe(update) nil end # Read this after the terminal has sent an update. snapshot = terminals.terminal(session_id, terminal_id) output = snapshot.try(&.output) The store keeps the newest 1 MiB of output per terminal by default. Set output_byte_limit: to choose a different byte budget, or zero to keep terminal state without output bytes. output is a detached byte slice when output is available. It can begin in the middle of a UTF-8 character or terminal sequence when the limit discards earlier bytes. Apply your display policy before rendering it. output_meta_raw describes the latest replacement snapshot. Chunk metadata is available on each TerminalOutputChunk update. The default terminal_limit: is 128 across all sessions. At capacity, observe returns false for new terminal IDs. The default terminal_metadata_byte_limit: is 64 KiB per terminal. A top-level _meta patch that would exceed this limit leaves the stored metadata unchanged. Use forget_session to discard one session's display history. For full replay of a session tree, clear the parent and each affected child first, or rebuild the display state in a fresh store. Stored capabilities reflect the reported display state. Use client.terminal_cancel for current cancellation checks. ACP v2 display-only terminals Repeat initialization On a v2 connection, call initialize_connection again before your first other request. Wait for each initialization to return before calling it again. Use the optional info, capabilities, and meta arguments to update what you advertise. Omitted arguments reuse the last successful offer. Pass meta: nil to clear the initialization metadata. The latest successful handshake takes effect on the connection. A JSON-RPC error from the Agent leaves the previous successful handshake active. A timeout or malformed response closes the connection because the Agent may have already applied the new handshake. ACP v2 Repeating Initialization Automatic version negotiation Use ACP.connect_negotiated to try ACP v2 Preview first. If the Agent selects v1, the connector closes the first connection and starts a fresh one with the v1 handshake. An initialization error or unknown version is returned to the caller. client = ACP.connect_negotiated("my-agent", ["--stdio"]) begin case client when ACP::V2::Client puts client.initialization_result.not_nil!.info.name when ACP::Client puts client.agent_info.try(&.name) || "ACP v1 Agent" end ensure client.close end The optional info applies to both handshakes. Advertise capabilities through v1_capabilities and v2_capabilities. To negotiate over a custom transport, pass a block to ACP.connect_negotiated that opens a fresh transport each time it is called. ACP Initialization Constructor .new ACP::Client.new( transport : ACP::Transport, client_name : String = "acp-crystal", client_version : String = ACP::VERSION, client_capabilities : ACP::Protocol::ClientCapabilities = ACP::Protocol::ClientCapabilities.new, client_info : ACP::Protocol::ClientInfo? = nil ) Parameter Type Default Description transport Transport -- The transport layer to use client_name String "acp-crystal" Client application name client_version String ACP::VERSION Client version string client_capabilities ClientCapabilities ClientCapabilities.new Advertised client capabilities client_info ClientInfo? nil Optional full implementation info, including display title and _meta When supplied, client_info supplies the name and version sent in the handshake. The same keyword is available on ACP.connect. Use the Transport interface to instrument or substitute the wire connection. Typed client methods can handle responses directly in the dispatcher. Lifecycle Methods #initialize_connection client.initialize_connection : ACP::Protocol::InitializeResult Performs the ACP handshake with the agent. Transitions state from Created to Initialized. Returns agent info and capabilities. #authenticate client.authenticate(method_id : String) : Nil client.authenticate(params : ACP::Protocol::AuthenticateParams) : ACP::Protocol::AuthenticateResult Authenticates with the agent using an advertised Agent-managed method. Call after initialize_connection if authentication is required. Use client.typed_auth_methods to inspect the available flows. Pass typed parameters to send request metadata and receive the Agent's result. Set meta_raw on the parameters or read it on the result for exact JSON values. #authenticate_terminal client.authenticate_terminal(method_id) { |method| ... } runs an advertised terminal login before session setup. Set auth: ACP::Protocol::ClientAuthCapabilities.new(terminal: true) in the client capabilities when your ProcessTransport can run the configured agent directly in an interactive terminal. The block receives TerminalAuthMethod#args and #env. Present them to the user and return true to approve the invocation. Use the returned Client for subsequent calls. It connects with the original process configuration, initializes, and carries over the previous callbacks and timeouts. A declined or unsuccessful login raises ACP::AuthenticationError and leaves the original connection available. See ACP Terminal Authentication. #logout client.logout(params : ACP::Protocol::LogoutParams = ACP::Protocol::LogoutParams.new) : ACP::Protocol::LogoutResult Ends the authenticated state (logout). Only call it when agent_capabilities.try(&.auth).try(&.logout?) is true. Active sessions may start failing with auth errors afterwards. Pass LogoutParams to attach request metadata. Both the parameters and result expose meta_raw for exact JSON values. #auth_status (draft) On v1 and v2, client.auth_status reads the Agent's authentication state when the auth.status capability is advertised. Register on_auth_status_update to receive changes from the Agent. state maps future values to unknown, and raw_state preserves the wire value. accounts describes the accounts for display and skips invalid entries. Use meta_raw on the status snapshot or an individual account to read extension metadata without rounding numbers. To attach exact metadata to the query, set AuthStatusParams#meta_raw=. Compare exact JSON values via meta_raw when differences beyond JSON::Any precision matter. ACP Authentication State Proposal #close client.close : Nil Closes the connection, stops the dispatcher fiber, and cleans up resources. Transitions state to Closed. Session Methods #session_new client.session_new( cwd : String, mcp_servers : Array(JSON::Any) = [] of JSON::Any, *, additional_directories : Array(String)? = nil, system_prompt : ACP::Protocol::SystemPrompt? = nil ) : ACP::Protocol::SessionNewResult Creates a new session. Transitions state to SessionActive. additional_directories (extra absolute workspace roots) and system_prompt (e.g. ACP::Protocol::SystemPrompt.append("...")) are omitted from the request when nil. Only pass them when the agent advertises sessionCapabilities.additionalDirectories? / sessionCapabilities.system_prompt?, and only use an override prompt when system_prompt.override? is true. session_load and session_resume take the same two keyword arguments; send the full root list and the original prompt again, since neither is restored implicitly. #session_load client.session_load( session_id : String, cwd : String, mcp_servers : Array(JSON::Any) = [] of JSON::Any, *, additional_directories : Array(String)? = nil, system_prompt : ACP::Protocol::SystemPrompt? = nil ) : ACP::Protocol::SessionLoadResult Resumes a previous session by ID. Pass typed setup parameters to session_new, session_load, session_resume, or session_fork to attach extension metadata. Use meta_raw on setup parameters, system prompts, and initial configuration options for exact JSON numbers. V2 initial configuration options also expose value_raw for custom values. MCP declarations, HTTP headers, and environment variables also expose meta_raw. Use mcp_servers_raw on v1 setup parameters to read or replace the exact server list. The existing mcp_servers accessor provides an editable JSON::Any view. ACP v1 request validation The client checks the Agent's advertised capabilities before calling session/load, session/resume, session/list, session/close, or session/delete. Images, audio, and embedded resources in prompts also require the matching capability. Text and resource links are available by default. Use absolute paths in the Agent's filesystem for session directories and MCP stdio executables. Additional roots, system prompts, and HTTP or SSE MCP servers require the Agent to advertise support. A system prompt accepts non-empty text content and uses append or a mode advertised by the Agent. For extensions that advertise custom modes through metadata, set client.on_system_prompt_mode to interpret the extension's declaration. The resolver receives the mode name and the Agent's system-prompt capability. The client raises InvalidStateError for missing capabilities and ArgumentError for invalid paths or content. ACP v1 Session Setup ACP v1 Prompt Turn The v1 and v2 clients accept typed parameters for session list, options, status, title, archive, unarchive, close, and delete requests. Set meta_raw on these parameters to send exact extension values. #session_status (draft) Call client.session_status(session_id) to query a session without attaching to it. The Agent advertises support through sessionCapabilities.status in v1 or session.status in v2. Session#status queries the wrapped v1 session ID. Pass meta: to include extension metadata in the request. status returns open for a session in memory and saved for a persisted session or a future status. raw_status preserves the Agent's value. In v2, state can also carry a foreground snapshot. A missing snapshot leaves the foreground state unknown. An unknown session ID raises an ACP::JsonRpcError with code -32002. ACP Session Status Proposal #session_options (draft) Call client.session_options(cwd) to preview configuration for a new session. For a saved session, use SessionOptionsParams.new(cwd, session_id: id). The Agent advertises this feature through sessionCapabilities.options in v1 or session.options in v2. V1 previews include modes when available. V2 previews can also include advisory slash commands. Pass chosen values as an ordered config_options: array of InitialSessionConfigOption values on session/new, v1 session/load, or session/resume. Use the protocol version's namespace. In v1, boolean choices require the Client's session.configOptions.boolean capability. Read the resulting configuration and, in v2, the available commands from the setup response. ACP Session Options Proposal #session_fork (draft) Call client.session_fork(source_id, cwd) when the Agent advertises sessionCapabilities.fork in v1 or session.fork in v2. The returned session_id identifies the new active session. V1 also exposes Session#fork(cwd), which returns a wrapper for the fork. Use SessionForkParams in the protocol version's namespace to supply extra workspace roots, MCP servers, a system prompt, or ordered initial settings. For a custom system prompt mode, check the Agent's extension advertisement before supplying the mode. Pass cursor_id: to fork at a cursor reported as forkable on the source session on this connection. A -32602 reply retires the fork grant used by that request. A later announcement can grant fork access again. The source session keeps its history and its other cursors. ACP Session Fork Proposal #session_set_title (draft) Call client.session_set_title(session_id, title) on v1 or v2 when the Agent advertises sessionCapabilities.title or session.title, respectively. The session can be inactive on the connection. Use result.title for display because the Agent can normalize the title before storing it. Session#set_title uses the wrapped v1 session ID. ACP Session Title Proposal #session_archive and #session_unarchive (draft) Call client.session_archive(session_id) to close a session and hide it from the default list while retaining its ID and saved conversation. Call client.session_unarchive(session_id) to restore it to the default list. Load or resume it separately before prompting. Both operations require the Agent's sessionCapabilities.archive capability in v1 or session.archive in v2. A missing session produces JSON-RPC error -32002. The v1 Session wrapper also exposes archive and unarchive. If a request times out, the Agent may still commit the change. Check the session's archive state in a later list response. #session_list Both protocol versions return usable sessions in the Agent's order, even when some entries are malformed. V2 entries use absolute workspace roots and RFC 3339 timestamps. The page and each entry expose exact extension metadata via meta_raw. Use has_more? to check for another page. An empty cursor is valid. Pass next_cursor and the original filters in the next request. ACP v1 session list ACP v2 session list Use client.session_list(archived: "only") in v1 or pass ACP::Protocol::V2::SessionListParams.new(archived: "only") in v2 to list archived sessions. Use "include" to list both archived and unarchived sessions. Preserve the filter when following next_cursor. The Agent reports the archive state as SessionInfo#archived. ACP Session Archive Proposal #session_delete client.session_delete(session_id : String) : ACP::Protocol::SessionDeleteResult Removes a session from the agent's session/list results. Only call it when sessionCapabilities.delete? is true. A -32002 answer counts as success. The client's cached active session is left alone; call forget_session if you deleted it. #session_prompt client.session_prompt( blocks : Array(ACP::Protocol::ContentBlock), session_id : String? = nil ) : ACP::Protocol::SessionPromptResult Sends content blocks as a prompt to the active session. Pass ACP::Protocol::SessionPromptParams to specify a session and include extension metadata. Set meta_raw to keep exact JSON numbers. Stdio preserves these values, and custom transports can implement send_wire. #session_prompt_text client.session_prompt_text( text : String, session_id : String? = nil ) : ACP::Protocol::SessionPromptResult Convenience method to send a single text prompt. #session_cancel client.session_cancel(session_id : String? = nil) : Nil Cancels an in-progress generation. Pass ACP::Protocol::SessionCancelParams and set meta_raw to send exact JSON metadata in v1 or v2. V2 tool_call_cancel and terminal_cancel also accept their typed cancellation parameters with exact metadata. #session_set_mode client.session_set_mode( mode_id : String, session_id : String? = nil ) : Nil Switches the session to an advertised mode. Read the available modes and the current selection with client.session_modes(session_id). Omit the session ID to read or change the active session. Pass ACP::Protocol::SessionSetModeParams to include exact extension metadata with meta_raw and receive the Agent's acknowledgement. ACP v1 Session Modes #session_set_config_option client.session_set_config_option( config_id : String, value : String | Bool, session_id : String? = nil ) : ACP::Protocol::SessionSetConfigOptionResult Changes an option in the given or active session. Read the latest list with client.session_config_options(session_id). Pass an advertised value ID for a select option. To pass a Bool for a boolean option, advertise session.configOptions.boolean when initializing the client. Pass typed configuration parameters and set meta_raw to include exact extension metadata. V2 exposes value_raw to read or replace a custom value. Setup responses and configuration updates replace the session's option list as the client receives them. A successful configuration change also returns a complete list. Choice state is available until the session closes or the client forgets it. After a timed-out load, wait for the Agent's response or reconnect before requesting another load of the same session. ACP v1 Session Config Options #cancel_request client.cancel_request(request_id : ACP::Protocol::RequestId) : Nil Sends $/cancel_request for one of the client's outstanding requests. The agent still answers it, usually with a -32800 error (JsonRpcError#request_cancelled?). A request that hits its timeout is cancelled this way automatically. Use session_cancel to cancel a prompt turn. Pass ACP::Protocol::CancelRequestParams to include extension metadata. Extension Methods #ext_method client.ext_method( method : String, params : Hash(String, JSON::Any::Type)? = nil, timeout : Float64? = nil ) : JSON::Any Sends a custom extension request to the agent. #ext_notification client.ext_notification( method : String, params : Hash(String, JSON::Any::Type)? = nil ) : Nil Sends a custom extension notification (no response expected). State & Inspection Property Type Description state ClientState Current state (Created, Initialized, SessionActive, Closed) closed? Bool Whether the client is closed session_active? Bool Whether a session is active session_id String? Current session ID agent_capabilities AgentCapabilities? Negotiated agent capabilities agent_info AgentInfo? Agent metadata auth_methods Array(JSON::Any)? Editable view of the advertised methods auth_methods_raw Protocol::RawJson? Exact advertised methods and extension metadata typed_auth_methods Array(AuthenticationMethod) Supported protocol and terminal descriptors negotiated_protocol_version UInt16? Negotiated protocol version Configuration Property Type Default Description request_timeout Float64? 30.0 Default request timeout in seconds prompt_timeout Float64? 300.0 Prompt-specific timeout (5 minutes) Callbacks Callback Type Description on_update UpdateHandler? Handle streaming session updates on_request_permission RequestPermissionHandler? Handle v1 permission requests with exact tool data on_agent_request AgentRequestHandler? Handle agent-initiated requests on_notification NotificationHandler? Handle non-update notifications on_disconnect (-> Nil)? Called on connection loss Return Protocol::RequestPermissionResult.selected(option_id) or Protocol::RequestPermissionResult.cancelled from on_request_permission. The callback receives RequestPermissionParams with the original request ID. The tool call exposes raw_input_raw, raw_output_raw, content_raw, and locations_raw for values that need exact JSON. Its meta_raw accessor also preserves exact extension values, as do those on the request and its options. A selected ID must appear in the Agent's original options. Invalid results or selections return JSON-RPC -32603. Set meta_raw for exact metadata on the result or outcome_raw for an exact decision object. Over stdio, repeated permission option fields return -32602 before the callback runs. With on_request_permission unset, on_agent_request handles representable permission requests and returns the JSON form of the same result. Without a registered handler, the client returns a cancelled outcome. ACP v1 Permissions For an accepted URL elicitation, on_elicitation_complete receives the matching completion once. If no typed handler is set, the matching notification goes to on_notification. ACP v1 URL Completion For v1 compaction updates, advertise session.compaction in the client capabilities. Read CompactionUpdate#summary_raw for exact replacement content and typed_summary for usable blocks. The summary_present? flag distinguishes an omitted summary from an explicit clear. On a CompactionSummaryChunkUpdate, the exact appended block is in content_raw, and the chunk's own metadata is in meta_raw. ACP v1 session compaction Subagent Sessions Set subagents: ACP::Protocol::SubagentCapabilities.new in the client capabilities before initialization to receive child session announcements and session-directed messages. Use the outer params.session_id for updates and request attribution, and SubagentUpdate#session_id for the announced child. Method Result subagent(session_id) Current child state and permissions, or nil subagents(parent_id) Immediate children announced under that parent session_workspace(session_id) Effective working directory and additional directories, or nil SubagentSession#cancel? indicates when session_cancel(child_id) is available. Other requests for the child raise ACP::InvalidStateError. Agent requests still reach their existing handlers with their original session IDs. Apply your workspace and permission policy to those requests. Use subagent(id) for confirmed state. During session/load, typed callbacks have before_load_response? set for the parent and its descendants. Treat child state, capabilities, and configuration in those updates as history. During session/resume, updates may arrive before the response. The client publishes effective state and cancellation permission when the resume succeeds. In v1, SessionMessageUpdate reports a message between sessions, and SessionMessageChunkUpdate appends one content block. Both expose exact extension metadata through meta_raw. On message updates, an omitted _meta leaves the stored metadata in place, null clears it, and an object replaces it. Check meta_present? to distinguish the updates. ACP v1 Subagents MCP-over-ACP (draft) Register an MCP handler on an initialized ACP client and include its declaration in session setup. The Agent must advertise mcpCapabilities.acp in v1 or session.mcp.acp in v2. A registration can be declared in multiple sessions on the same connection. server = client.register_mcp_server("workspace-tools") do |context| handle_workspace_mcp_request(context) end # With ACP::V2::Client wire_server = ACP::Protocol::V2::McpServer.acp(server) session = client.session_new(ACP::Protocol::V2::SessionNewParams.new( Dir.current, mcp_servers: [wire_server])) With ACP::Client v1, pass [server.to_json_any] as the mcp_servers list. The Agent can call a registered handler before the session setup response arrives. The handler receives ACP::McpRequestContext and returns a MessageMcpResponse.success(result) or .failure(mcp_error). Use McpJson.from_json to pass exact JSON for arguments, results, or opaque multi-round-trip state. Handlers implement the MCP methods they expose and apply authorization and subscription filters. The binding validates the MCP 2026-07-28 request metadata, routes context.notify to the active operation, and preserves inner MCP errors separately from ACP binding failures. Use context.cancellation or context.cancelled? to stop work and finish cleanup before returning. Unregistering a server or closing its connection signals cancellation to the affected handlers. Set mcp_request_limit: on either client to change the default of 32 active operations. The binding limits individual frames to 16 MiB, outer ACP IDs to 1 KiB, and retained input and queued output to 32 MiB each. A handler may have one notification waiting to write at a time. The connection closes if its bounded rejection queue fills. Stdio preserves exact JSON frames. Custom transports can return WireFrame with exact_params: true and override send_wire to preserve exact JSON in both directions. MCP-over-ACP Proposal Model providers (draft) After initialization, call providers_list if the Agent advertises agentCapabilities.providers in v1 or capabilities.providers in v2. Each entry reports the provider ID, its supported API protocols, whether the Agent requires it, and its current routing. A missing current value indicates a disabled provider. The routing summary carries the protocol and base URL. Call providers_set(SetProviderParams.new(provider_id, api_type, base_url, headers: headers)) to replace a provider's full configuration. Use the wire types in the protocol version's namespace. Supply the full intended header map with each replacement. The Agent owns routing and decides when changes apply to existing sessions. providers_disable(provider_id) queries the Agent's current provider list and rejects the operation if that provider is required. These methods apply to the Agent process. Built-in stdio frame logs redact provider parameters and their replies, including late or repeated replies. Once the log keeps track of more than 256 provider request IDs, it redacts all response payloads for that connection. Applications receive the Agent's JSON-RPC errors, including any data the Agent returns. Provider requests, replies, list entries, and routing summaries expose meta for values representable as JSON::Any and meta_raw for the original metadata, including full numeric precision. To send metadata outside the range or precision of JSON::Any, set meta_raw on the request and use a transport that supports exact JSON frames. ACP v1 draft schema · ACP v2 draft schema Agent Skills (v2 draft) Advertise commands: CommandsCapabilities.new(skill: CommandsSkillCapabilities.new) on Protocol::V2::ClientSessionCapabilities and pass it as session: on the v2 client capabilities. Read negotiated skills with session_available_commands(session_id).try(&.compact_map(&.skill)). Setup responses, command updates, and session_options previews also expose typed_available_skills. Each skill has a name, description, and optional path on the Agent's filesystem. When the user selects a skill, put its name in Protocol::V2::SkillReference.new(name) and send it through SessionPromptParams.new. Use Array(Protocol::V2::PromptContentBlock) to mix references with other typed content. An Agent that advertises session.prompt.skill accepts one reference as the first block. With session.prompt.skill.inline, references can appear anywhere. The client checks the session's current list before sending a new skill reference. To retry a keyed submission, call session_prompt(original_params, retry_submission: true) with the same prompt and idempotency_key. The Agent can then acknowledge an earlier submission after the command list has changed. In user-message updates, skill_references and skill_reference expose references in full messages and chunks, including during replay. Use meta_raw to read or set exact metadata on a skill reference. It stays with the reference when submitted as typed prompt content. ACP Agent Skills Proposal Prompt suggestions (draft) Opt in by setting prompt_suggestions: PromptSuggestionsCapabilities.new on the ClientSessionCapabilities for your protocol version. Pass that group as session: on ClientCapabilities. An empty prompt suggestion capability supports text and resource links. Add the image:, audio:, or embedded_context: markers to offer those content types when the Agent also supports them. In v1, read Protocol::PromptSuggestionsUpdate from on_update. In v2, read Protocol::V2::PromptSuggestionsUpdate from note.update.typed. Treat the list as a replacement for that session's current suggestions. An empty list withdraws the previous suggestions. Typed updates keep compatible candidates in the Agent's order and skip entire unusable candidates. Start with an empty list when you open or restore a session. After the user accepts a suggestion, pass its prompt to session_prompt in v1. In v2, pass prompt_raw to Protocol::V2::SessionPromptParams.new(session_id, suggestion.prompt_raw) to retain the original block fields and exact numbers. Call the request outside the dispatcher callback. Both versions expose exact update and suggestion metadata through meta_raw. The generic on_notification callback only offers candidates whose prompt fits in JSON::Any. Use the typed on_update callback to receive the full list with exact values. ACP Prompt Suggestions Proposal Session cursors (draft) On v1, opt in with ClientSessionCapabilities.new(cursors: SessionCursorsCapabilities.new) in the client's session capabilities. On v2, cursor updates are available automatically. They arrive through on_update as Protocol::CursorUpdate in v1 and through update.typed in v2. Use client.session_cursor(session_id, cursor_id) or client.session_cursors(session_id) to read the current snapshots. Their IDs are opaque and session-scoped. Each snapshot keeps the first reported anchor and the latest capabilities. Use anchor.known_position? and the transcript's entity IDs to decide where to display a cursor. Full replays rebuild the stored cursors, including announced child sessions. In v1, new snapshots become available when session/load succeeds. In v2, each session's replay_complete publishes its snapshots and starts applying live cursor updates. Until those boundaries, lookups return the previous snapshots. Use raw_meta_field for exact metadata values outside the range of JSON::Any. Full replays can supply updated entity IDs for existing cursor anchors. Closing a session or resuming without replay preserves its cursors. ACP Session Cursors Proposal Typed Client Method Handlers For ACP v1, advertise file reads, file writes, and terminal support before initialization. The client handles fs/read_text_file and fs/write_text_file according to their separate capability flags. clientCapabilities.terminal enables the terminal methods as a group. Requests outside the advertisement return -32601 before reaching either the typed handler or on_agent_request. File paths and any supplied terminal working directory must be absolute in POSIX or Windows syntax. File reads use one-based line numbers. Terminal environment entries require string name and value fields. Malformed parameters return -32602 before either callback. Typed request parameters provide exact extension metadata through meta_raw, and CreateTerminalParams#env_raw retains the complete environment array. ACP v1 File System ACP v1 Terminals Call client.session_workspace(params.session_id) to look up the Agent-side cwd and additional_directories in either callback. ACP v1 records the roots from successful new, load, resume, and fork replies, including raw requests and sessions without subagents. A successful reattachment replaces the root set. A reattachment timeout clears the lookup until a setup succeeds. A confirmed close or archive, local forget_session, and disconnection also clear it. The lookup returns nil when the workspace is unknown. Announced subagents can inherit roots from their parent. Apply your application's access policy using these roots. The ACP file system spec recommends checking resolved paths at the time of use and comparing them by path component. ACP v1 Workspace Root Security Use meta_raw= to attach exact JSON metadata to typed file and terminal results, including TerminalExitStatus. Stdio preserves the original number tokens. Custom transports that cannot preserve an exact reply return -32603 to the Agent. ACP v1 Extension Metadata For ACP v1 file and terminal methods, on_agent_request must return a result object with the method's required fields. Return {} for an empty successful acknowledgement. Malformed results return -32603. Additional result fields and explicit ACP::JsonRpcError replies pass through. Return a fresh terminalId for every successful terminal/create on the connection. Subsequent terminal requests must use that ID with its creating session. With a handler registered, unknown, retired, and other-session IDs return -32002 before dispatch. A duplicate creation ID returns -32603 and invalidates that ID for the connection. terminal/kill keeps the terminal available for output and exit status. Your release callback must stop the command if it is still running and free its resources. Successful release invalidates the ID. A confirmed session close or archive, or a local forget_session, also clears the retired attachment's terminal bindings. The application owns terminal processes and their cleanup, including cleanup when a creation reply cannot be delivered. ACP v1 Terminals The client applies the original terminal/create output byte limit to typed and generic terminal/output replies. It replaces invalid UTF-8 bytes with replacement characters, then keeps the newest complete characters that fit. When the client records truncation from a validated output snapshot, later snapshots of that terminal keep truncated set to true. The application controls its terminal capture buffer and can enforce the same limit while collecting output. ACP v1 Terminal Output Limit Handler Params Type Result Type Description on_read_text_file ReadTextFileParams ReadTextFileResult Handle fs/read_text_file on_write_text_file WriteTextFileParams WriteTextFileResult Handle fs/write_text_file on_create_terminal CreateTerminalParams CreateTerminalResult Handle terminal/create on_terminal_output TerminalOutputParams TerminalOutputResult Handle terminal/output on_release_terminal ReleaseTerminalParams ReleaseTerminalResult Handle terminal/release on_wait_for_terminal_exit WaitForTerminalExitParams WaitForTerminalExitResult Handle terminal/wait_for_exit on_kill_terminal KillTerminalParams KillTerminalResult Handle terminal/kill on_create_elicitation CreateElicitationParams CreateElicitationResult Handle elicitation/create on_elicitation_complete CompleteElicitationParams Nil Handle the elicitation/complete notification (else on_notification) Set client_capabilities.elicitation to the modes on_create_elicitation handles. A request for a mode that isn't advertised there is answered with -32602 and never reaches the handler. Each agent request runs its handler in its own fiber, so a handler may block (e.g. waiting on the user) without holding up responses or notifications, but request handlers may run concurrently with each other and with notification callbacks. on_update / on_notification still run in arrival order on the dispatcher fiber, so they must not wait on a request of their own (for example session_set_mode): its response can't be read until the callback returns, so the call times out (or, with a nil timeout, hangs for good). Make such calls from another fiber (spawn). A request with no matching handler, including an unknown _-prefixed extension method, is answered with -32601 Method not found. A handler that raises ACP::JsonRpcError is answered with that error's code, message and data (for example -32002 for a missing file or unknown terminal); any other exception becomes -32603. When the Agent cancels a permission request, the Client answers with the cancelled outcome. A cancelled v2 elicitation gets the cancel action. Other requests that only read or wait, such as fs/read_text_file, terminal/output, and terminal/wait_for_exit, are answered with -32800. Those handlers' late answers are dropped. Handlers for writes, terminal creation, and extension requests still answer the original request. Valid cancellations are also passed to on_notification so the application can stop the work. ACP v2 delivers this callback for outstanding requests from the Agent. Cancellation IDs retain their number or string type, and ambiguous IDs are ignored. Use CancelRequestParams#meta_raw when decoding the notification JSON directly. ACP v2 request cancellation

title: Errors
content: Overview All acp.cr errors inherit from ACP::Error, which itself inherits from Crystal's Exception. Errors are organized by category: transport, protocol, state, and request-level. Error Hierarchy ACP::Error Base class for all acp.cr errors. begin # any ACP operation rescue ex : ACP::Error puts ex.message end ACP::TransportError Transport-level failure (e.g., broken pipe, IO error). rescue ex : ACP::TransportError puts "Transport failed: #{ex.message}" ACP::ConnectionClosedError The connection is closed: raised by a call made after it closed, and by a request still waiting when the agent exits or close runs. rescue ex : ACP::ConnectionClosedError puts "Connection lost" ACP::TransportTimeoutError A transport-level operation timed out. The built-in transports never raise it; a request that times out raises RequestTimeoutError. rescue ex : ACP::TransportTimeoutError puts "Transport timeout" ACP::ProtocolError A protocol-level issue occurred, such as a response without exactly one result or error field. A null result is valid at the JSON-RPC layer. Replies must use the same integer ID as the Client's request. A reply with an ID written as a string, decimal, or exponent leaves the request pending until a matching reply or the usual timeout. JSON-RPC 2.0 response IDs rescue ex : ACP::ProtocolError puts "Protocol error: #{ex.message}" ACP::VersionMismatchError The agent's protocol version is incompatible. rescue ex : ACP::VersionMismatchError puts "Version mismatch: #{ex.message}" ACP::InvalidStateError An operation was attempted in the wrong client state. rescue ex : ACP::InvalidStateError puts "Invalid state: #{ex.message}" ACP::JsonRpcError A JSON-RPC 2.0 error was returned by the agent. Use data_raw to read the exact JSON data, including numbers outside the range of JSON::Any. The data accessor exposes representable values. Use unsupported_protocol_version? for the ACP v2 negotiation error -32022. Its data can be decoded as ACP::Protocol::V2::UnsupportedProtocolVersionData to inspect the requested and supported versions. rescue ex : ACP::JsonRpcError puts "Error code: #{ex.code}" puts "Error message: #{ex.message}" ACP::SessionNotFoundError The referenced session does not exist. The client never raises it itself: an agent reports an unknown session as a JsonRpcError with code -32002 (resource_not_found?). rescue ex : ACP::SessionNotFoundError puts "Session not found" ACP::NoActiveSessionError An operation requiring an active session was attempted without one. rescue ex : ACP::NoActiveSessionError puts "No active session" ACP::AuthenticationError authenticate_terminal raises this error when the user declines the terminal invocation or the login process exits unsuccessfully. Agent-managed authentication errors arrive as JsonRpcError. An agent can use -32000 (auth_required?) to request authentication. rescue ex : ACP::AuthenticationError puts "Auth failed: #{ex.message}" ACP::RequestTimeoutError A request exceeded its timeout duration. rescue ex : ACP::RequestTimeoutError puts "Request timed out" ACP::RequestCancelledError A request was cancelled before completion. The client never raises it itself: an agent answers a cancelled request with a JsonRpcError with code -32800 (request_cancelled?). rescue ex : ACP::RequestCancelledError puts "Request cancelled" Error Codes Standard JSON-RPC 2.0 error codes and ACP-specific codes: Constant Value Description PARSE_ERROR -32700 Invalid JSON received INVALID_REQUEST -32600 Invalid JSON-RPC request METHOD_NOT_FOUND -32601 Method does not exist INVALID_PARAMS -32602 Invalid method parameters INTERNAL_ERROR -32603 Internal error AUTH_REQUIRED -32000 Authentication required RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND -32002 Requested resource not found

title: PromptBuilder
content: Overview ACP::PromptBuilder provides a builder pattern for constructing arrays of ContentBlock objects. It supports text, images, audio, embedded resources, and resource links. Constructor ACP::PromptBuilder.new Creates a new empty builder. Methods #text builder.text(content : String) : ACP::PromptBuilder Adds a text content block. Returns self for chaining. #image builder.image( data : String, mime_type : String? = nil ) : ACP::PromptBuilder Adds a base64-encoded image content block. #audio builder.audio( data : String, mime_type : String? = nil ) : ACP::PromptBuilder Adds a base64-encoded audio content block. #resource builder.resource( uri : String, text : String, mime_type : String? = nil ) : ACP::PromptBuilder Adds an embedded resource content block with inline text content. #resource_link(path) builder.resource_link( path : String, mime_type : String? = nil ) : ACP::PromptBuilder Adds a resource link from a file path. Automatically converts to a file:// URI. #resource_link(uri, name) builder.resource_link( uri : String, name : String, mime_type : String? = nil ) : ACP::PromptBuilder Adds a resource link with an explicit URI and display name. #build builder.build : Array(ACP::Protocol::ContentBlock) Returns the assembled array of content blocks. #size builder.size : Int32 Returns the number of content blocks. #empty? builder.empty? : Bool Returns true if no content blocks have been added. Example builder = ACP::PromptBuilder.new builder .text("Review the following files for security issues:") .resource_link("/src/auth.cr", "text/x-crystal") .resource_link("/src/api.cr", "text/x-crystal") .text("Focus on input validation and SQL injection risks.") blocks = builder.build result = session.prompt(blocks)

title: Protocol Types
content: Overview The ACP::Protocol module contains all JSON-RPC 2.0 and ACP schema types. All types use JSON::Serializable and many use discriminated unions for polymorphic deserialization. Enumerations StopReason enum ACP::Protocol::StopReason EndTurn MaxTokens MaxTurnRequests Refusal Cancelled end ToolKind enum ACP::Protocol::ToolKind Read Edit Delete Move Search Execute Think Fetch SwitchMode Other end ToolCallStatus enum ACP::Protocol::ToolCallStatus Pending InProgress Completed Failed end PermissionOptionKind enum ACP::Protocol::PermissionOptionKind AllowOnce AllowAlways RejectOnce RejectAlways end PlanEntryPriority enum ACP::Protocol::PlanEntryPriority High Medium Low end PlanEntryStatus enum ACP::Protocol::PlanEntryStatus Pending InProgress Completed end SessionConfigOptionCategory enum ACP::Protocol::SessionConfigOptionCategory Mode Model ThoughtLevel Other end Role enum ACP::Protocol::Role Assistant User end Content Blocks Content blocks are used to construct prompts. They form a discriminated union (ContentBlock): Type Description TextContentBlock Plain text with optional annotations ImageContentBlock Base64 image with MIME type AudioContentBlock Base64 audio with MIME type ResourceContentBlock Embedded resource (URI + content) ResourceLinkContentBlock Resource link with metadata FileContentBlock Backward-compatible alias for ResourceLinkContentBlock ACP v2 resource links expose icons as Array(Protocol::Icon)?. Each icon carries src, optional MIME type and sizes, and an open theme string. Use meta_raw for exact extension metadata. When displaying icons, apply the ACP icon-fetching rules to the supplied source URI. ACP v2 resource links · ACP URI guidance Use size_bytes for non-negative sizes through UInt64::MAX. The existing size accessor retains the signed view used by ACP v1. Pass icons: to a typed link or either PromptBuilder#resource_link overload. The v2 client sends exact prompt content with StdioTransport. Custom transports can override send_wire to support exact prompt frames. Use ContentBlock.from_v2_json to decode ACP v2 display content directly. Custom and future types yield an UnknownContentBlock. Its type, custom?, and raw accessors expose the discriminator, the extension namespace check, and the complete JSON payload. Standard types use their typed decoders. User-message skill references use the dedicated skill_reference and skill_references methods. ACP v2 content types V2 full messages and session-directed messages expose content_blocks for display blocks and content_raw for the complete replacement. Ambiguous optional fields are treated as omitted. An explicit null clears the corresponding value. Message and compaction summary chunks provide to_content_chunk with exact meta_raw. Read a serialized v2 wrapper with ContentChunk.from_v2_json. Message chunks also expose content_raw. A message with an ambiguous ID or a chunk with unusable content has no typed update. The data remains available in SessionUpdateParams#raw. ACP v2 message IDs Tool results and summary chunks provide content_block. Compaction updates expose typed_summary and summary_raw. List helpers skip malformed blocks and keep the usable blocks in wire order. The mutable JSON::Any views expose representable fields. Updating or reordering existing blocks preserves their other exact fields. A replacement block uses the supplied JSON::Any value. Tool Call Content Types for tool call content within updates: Type Description ToolCallContentBlock Wraps a standard content block ToolCallDiff File modification diff (path, oldText, newText) ToolCallTerminal Embedded terminal reference by ID ToolCallSessionReference Display reference to a session by ID ToolCallLocation File location tracking (path, line) Session Update Types Session updates are received via the on_update callback. They form a discriminated union (SessionUpdate): Type Key Fields AgentMessageChunkUpdate content : JSON::Any, text : String, message_id : String? AgentThoughtChunkUpdate content : JSON::Any, text : String, message_id : String? ToolCallUpdate tool_call_id : String, title : String, kind : String?, status : String? ToolCallStatusUpdate tool_call_id : String, status : String?, title : String? PlanUpdate entries : Array(PlanEntry) for the session's baseline checklist IdentifiedPlanUpdate plan : PlanUpdateContent (needs plan) PlanRemovedUpdate plan_id : String (needs plan) SubagentUpdate Child session_id with optional capability, state, and workspace patches SessionMessageUpdate message_id with participant, linked transcript ID, and content patches SessionMessageChunkUpdate message_id and a single typed content block to append UserMessageChunkUpdate content : JSON::Any, text : String, message_id : String? AvailableCommandsUpdate available_commands : Array(AvailableCommand) CurrentModeUpdate current_mode_id : String ConfigOptionUpdate config_options : Array(JSON::Any), typed_config_options : Array(ConfigOption) NoticeUpdate severity : String, title : String, description : String? (needs session.notices) CompactionUpdate compaction_id : String, status : String, summary : Array(JSON::Any)?, error : String?, summary_present?, error_present?, typed_summary (needs session.compaction) CompactionSummaryChunkUpdate compaction_id : String, content : JSON::Any, text : String (needs session.compaction) Use to_content_chunk on agent message, user message, and thought updates to convert their payload to a typed ContentChunk with the same message_id and extension metadata. Use content_raw and meta_raw to read exact v1 content and chunk metadata when values exceed JSON::Any. The content accessor provides the editable JSON::Any view. CompactionUpdate's summary, error and _meta are patches. If a field is omitted, the stored value stays as it is. If it is null, the value is cleared. Both cases read as nil, so use summary_present? / error_present? / meta_present? to tell them apart. Set plan: ACP::Protocol::PlanCapabilities.new in the client capabilities to receive identified plans. In your callback, replace the entire plan for {params.session_id, update.plan.plan_id} on each IdentifiedPlanUpdate. PlanItems contains entries. PlanMarkdown contains the complete content and an optional absolute path. On PlanRemovedUpdate, drop the matching plan for that session. The client ignores removals of IDs it has not received. See ACP Agent Plan. The SubagentUpdate and SessionMessageUpdate types expose *_present? methods for patch fields. An omitted field retains its previous value and an explicit null clears it. A SubagentState retains extension fields in json_unmapped, including any payload for a future state or stop reason. See ACP Subagents. Token Usage SessionPromptResult#usage exposes the optional draft v1 token report. The Agent sends its accumulated counts with the completed prompt result. Usage provides total_tokens, input_tokens, and output_tokens as UInt64, plus optional reasoning and cache counts. In v2, use StateUpdate#usage or StateSnapshot#usage for the token counts the Agent reported for completed foreground work. A repeated or replayed snapshot may carry the same usage and must not be counted again. ACP v2 Preview Wire Types ACP::Protocol::V2 contains preview wire types for initialization, capabilities, authentication, session setup, configuration changes, and prompt acknowledgements. It includes method names and structured unsupported-version error data. Unknown authentication variants preserve their payload for inspection or forwarding. ACP::V2::Client uses these types for v2 connections. Client API See ACP v2 Initialization. Use ReplayFrom.start in v2 SessionResumeParams to request replay from the start of retained history. The v2 SessionPromptParams accepts an optional idempotency_key, and its response carries the inserted message_id. The Agent reports completion through a later session update. See ACP v2 Prompt Lifecycle. V2::SessionUpdateParams retains the original update fields. Its update.typed accessor decodes foreground state, message upserts and chunks, and replay completion. Use StateUpdate#idle? and #stop_reason to inspect foreground completion. An absent or invalid background list represents unreported work, and an empty list reports that no work is running. Unknown background kinds still count as work. States and background entries expose their exact fields through raw and meta_raw. State snapshots also expose background_raw, usage_raw, and error_raw for their reported payloads. ACP v2 background work For v2 upserts, meta_present? distinguishes a supplied patch from omission, and meta_raw exposes the exact metadata object. Use apply_metadata_raw(previous) to apply the patch to an existing RawJson? snapshot. Null clears the snapshot or removes an individual key, and other values replace their key whole. Use apply_metadata for a Hash(String, JSON::Any) view. ACP v2 metadata patches update.typed also decodes tool-call and Agent-owned terminal updates and chunks. Terminal snapshots and chunks expose decoded bytes through bytes. The *_present? methods on upserts identify fields the update supplies, including explicit clears. Typed v2 display content validates Base64 media and absolute resource URIs. An invalid optional image URI leaves the image data available. Embedded text remains available when a sibling blob is invalid. Resource links omit invalid sizes and icon entries. Display icons use credential-free HTTPS URLs or Base64 image data URIs. Raw accessors retain the original values for inspection. ACP v2 content Terminal updates treat malformed optional fields as omitted. A concrete exit_status still marks an exit when its code and signal are unknown. Output snapshots and chunks validate standard Base64 on receipt. Decode each chunk independently with bytes and append the decoded bytes in receive order. A snapshot replaces the accumulated output. Repeated capability fields clear the cancel grant for the addressed terminal. ACP v2 display-only terminals Tool-call updates and permission tool-call subjects treat malformed optional fields as omitted. Content and locations arrays replace the previous list with their usable entries in wire order. Explicit null and empty arrays clear the list. Tool-call locations require absolute Agent-side paths. An invalid optional line leaves just the path, and meta_raw exposes the location's exact extension metadata. ACP v2 Tool Calls Process ToolCallContentChunk in receive order with ToolCallUpdate. Append each chunk's item to the content for its tool call. A later update's present content field replaces or clears that list. Chunk metadata is scoped to the chunk. Streamed and replacement content use the same item validation and preserve custom and future payloads. An unusable chunk remains available in the raw notification. ToolCallStore applies both variants to track the current state. Tool-call state · ACP v2 streamed tool content ToolCallContent#diff exposes usable file changes in wire order and omits entries with conflicting destination paths. It returns nil when no usable changes remain. A malformed optional patch object leaves the structured changes available. Use changes for affected paths, git_patch to select patches labeled with ACP's standard format, and patch to inspect other formats. Tool content and individual file changes expose open fields through raw. Diffs, patches, file changes, tool content, and content chunks expose exact metadata through meta_raw. ACP v2 Tool Calls Typed child-session announcements and the child cache use the same patch rules. Malformed optional title, description, capability, or state values are treated as omitted. A repeated capability field clears the cancel grant. Child workspace values use absolute Agent-side paths. An explicit null restores inheritance for that workspace field, and an empty additional-directory list overrides inheritance. The cached SubagentSession#meta_raw exposes the exact association metadata after applying key-level patches. ACP v2 Subagents Session-directed messages keep independent local IDs in each session. sender_session_id, recipient_session_id, sender_message_id, and recipient_message_id patch independently. A malformed or ambiguous optional field leaves the previous value in place. Chunk content appends in receive order, and a present content patch replaces or clears the accumulated list. Chunk metadata stays scoped to the chunk. Raw notifications retain the received content and its exact values. ACP v2 session-directed messages SessionInfoUpdate, UsageUpdate, and CompactionUpdate distinguish omitted fields from clears and apply metadata patches by key. Invalid optional fields leave the previous value in place. updated_at preserves the reported RFC 3339 string. UsageUpdate#cost_raw preserves the original cumulative cost amount and metadata. cost exposes its typed Float64 projection. A compaction summary patch replaces or clears accumulated content, and usable summary chunks append in receive order. Raw notifications retain the original values. ACP v2 compaction and usage V2 notices use NoticeUpdate and expose the original severity, the required title, and optional description. They are live events with no capability requirement. Both notices and ReplayCompleteUpdate expose exact event metadata through meta_raw. Each replay marker applies to its own session, including during child-session replay. ACP v2 session notices ACP v2 replay completion V2::PlanUpdate#plan exposes the plan ID and the full representation as raw. Its typed accessor returns a checklist or a Markdown plan, and checklists keep valid entries in order. Replace the whole plan for the given session and plan ID, including when the representation is unknown. PlanRemovedUpdate removes a known plan. The v2 client ignores removals for plan IDs it has not received in that session. Register your callback before creating or resuming the session. The client bounds the provisional IDs it tracks before creation completes. Use on_update to receive plans containing exact values outside JSON::Any. ACP v2 Agent Plan Session setup, option previews, option changes, and configuration updates expose typed_config_options and config_options_raw. The typed view keeps valid options in Agent order, including unrecognized option types. The raw array retains the received values until the projected list is edited. ConfigOption#raw preserves the option's extension fields. Select options expose flat or grouped choices through select_options. ACP v2 configuration options Configuration lists, groups, and individual values retain exact JSON metadata. Use ConfigOptionGroup#options_raw or meta_raw to read values outside JSON::Any. Session setup, option previews, and command updates expose available_commands_raw and typed_available_commands. The raw list preserves the received entries and reflects edits to the projected list. Replacing an input object also replaces its previous extension data. The typed list skips duplicate names and retains unrecognized command types for inspection. Use slash_command? to identify slash commands and input for their input specification. Command inputs and typed skills expose exact metadata through meta_raw. ACP v2 slash commands Capabilities ClientCapabilities ACP::Protocol::ClientCapabilities.new( fs : FsCapabilities? = nil, terminal : Bool = false, session : ClientSessionCapabilities? = nil, elicitation : ElicitationCapabilities? = nil, plan : PlanCapabilities? = nil, subagents : SubagentCapabilities? = nil, auth : ClientAuthCapabilities? = nil ) Field Type Description fs FsCapabilities? File system capabilities terminal? Bool Terminal support session ClientSessionCapabilities? compaction, notices and config_options.boolean; each one is opt-in elicitation ElicitationCapabilities? Supported elicitation/create modes (form, url) plan PlanCapabilities? Support for identified plan updates and removals subagents SubagentCapabilities? Support for child sessions and session-directed messages auth ClientAuthCapabilities? Opt-in terminal authentication Nothing is advertised by default. Only set a capability once the client handles it. FsCapabilities ACP::Protocol::FsCapabilities.new( read_text_file : Bool = false, write_text_file : Bool = false ) AgentCapabilities Field Type Description load_session Bool? Session loading support prompt_capabilities PromptCapabilities? Prompt format support mcp_capabilities McpCapabilities? MCP support session_capabilities SessionCapabilities? PromptCapabilities Field Type Description image Bool? Image content support audio Bool? Audio content support embedded_context Bool? A form request has requested_schema : ElicitationSchema, and a URL request has elicitation_id and url. A session-scoped request has session_id and may have tool_call_id; a request-scoped one has request_id.
